reviews.review: game is a blast, exceeded my expectations. seems very simple at first however tons of content, new items, enemies and places to explore.
this game is really fun and has fun mechanics and is also a good game that i like to play it is good and fun yeah good game i like alot i recomend

++Variety of environments, abilities, lore
++Great soundtrack
++Challenging and great to overcome
++Real feeling of power once you get going
++Multiplayer
++Artifact codes are a cool puzzle
++Robust modding support

--Game can end up feeling shallow after a time, as the largely global availability of items (take a run long enough and you will have several copies of every item in the game) takes away almost any semblance of "builds" and the sheer power of items makes successful runs feel very similar each time, even between vastly different survivors. Eclipse mode alleviates this somewhat, but i'd still say Risk of Rain 2 lacks in longevity compared to most roguelikes.

Above is my main con, below are some more specific design criticisms:

--Difficulty of the enemies and bosses can fluctuate quite wildly and be at odds with how early they are encountered.
--Elite common enemies are often the most dangerous ones on the field, often eclipsing even the bosses in threat, Some of these elites not only do immense damage that can end runs in a single hit, but also bypass the game's built-in one-shot protection, a mechanic which's mere presence i think is already indicative of design problems.
--Several unlockables are behind challenges that practically force you to play on the easiest difficulty because of how immensely frustrating and often time-consuming they would be to do on difficulties the game is actually designed to be played at.
--Some of the items barred behind these challenges are some of the most powerful in the game. A number of alternate abilities, many also behind these challenges, are essentially direct upgrades to the abilities they're replacing.
--The rarity of items is sometimes at odds with their usefulness, such as critical chance or bleed damage being common items, while uncommon items include slight slowdown on hit or spawning pitiful turrets from chests. While this works in the sense that common items are supposed to be stacked more, the power of certain commons can end up in situations where receiving uncommon items is the unlucky outcome.
--Lunar coins go from being an actual limited resource at the start to being virtually unlimited and more accessible than the normal per-stage money after simply enough playtime

In the end it is a fun game that i can recommend, but it is held back by a number of frustrating elements as well as not having quite the same replayability as comparable games, especially given the price. If you're not certain you want it, wait for a sale.
